absent: Full PMU structure outside the routed tail, including earlier hooks, capabilities, and context numbers.
Complete overflow handler signature beyond the visible leading event parameter.
Bodies and error paths for validation, sync, snapshot, match, filter, and period hooks.
Event scheduling, rotation, throttling, and cross CPU migration algorithms.
Ring buffer structure, mapping lifecycle, wakeup thresholds, and signal delivery.
Tracepoint, ftrace, BPF program, cgroup, and security hook interactions beyond field presence.
Guest state provider implementations and mediated interrupt handling.
Numeric encodings for branch, sample, and memory attribute option bits tested by predicates.
Lock ordering across context, child, mapping, filter, and timer guards and interrupt safety beyond the stated assertions.
Lifetime and reclamation rules for references, RCU heads, and namespaces.

findings.text: PMU tail defines six optional hooks. Snapshot copies auxiliary data to an output handle in PMI context and reports bytes copied while remaining safe against preemption of start and stop. Validation checks hardware support for requested address filters in the calling process context and is explicitly unsynchronized. Sync translates generic filters into hardware state during start and may walk the filter list under caller serialization. Output match decides from open whether an event suits auxiliary output with zero meaning no match. Filter allows skipping a CPU for heterogeneous topologies. Period check validates a new period value from the period control.

Address filter actions form an ordered triple with stop at zero followed by start then filter. Stop and start control tracing windows while filter selects ranges to keep. The ordering is part of the interface so numeric succession from zero is relied upon.

An address filter links into a head list and carries a filesystem path plus byte offset plus byte size plus an action. Its head holds the list plus a raw spinlock plus a count of file backed filters. A separate range record holds only a start address plus a size for resolved virtual mappings.

Event lifetime uses seven ordered states from dead at negative five through revoked at negative four and exit at negative three and error at negative two and off at negative one to inactive at zero and active at one. Revoked means the owning unit is gone and must not be touched. Exit means the task died but inheritance continues. Error means a scheduling failure that still allows enabling.

Event capabilities use low bits zero through three. Bit zero marks software events. Bit one marks ability to read an active package. Bit two marks sibling awareness. Bit three marks read scope support.
Software event hash sizing uses eight bits for the index width, giving two hundred fifty six buckets as one shifted by that width.
Software event hash storage holds a fixed array of hash heads sized by the bucket count plus a deferred reclamation head for safe teardown.

Attach state uses ten single bit flags from one to five hundred twelve. One marks context, two group, four task, eight task data, sixteen global data, thirty two scheduler callback, sixty four child, one hundred twenty eight exclusive, two hundred fifty six callchain, five hundred twelve instruction trace.
A unit event list pairs a raw spinlock with a doubly linked list so iteration and mutation of pending unit events share one guard.

When checking is enabled the context assertion warns once if hard interrupts look enabled while the context mutex is not held, otherwise it expands to nothing. The sibling walker first performs that assertion and then walks the sibling linkage only when the starting event is its own group leader.

An event carries list linkage for context membership plus sibling and active links plus a red black node for pinned or flexible trees plus a separate migration link that preserves groups under RCU plus hash and active entry links plus sibling count. Grouping adds immutable capability bits plus intersected group capabilities plus generation plus leader pointer plus owning unit pointer plus private data plus state plus attach flags.

Accounting adds local and atomic counts plus enabled and running nanosecond totals plus a timestamp plus attribute block plus header size fields plus hardware state plus context and unit context pointers plus a long reference count plus atomic child totals. Family linkage adds a child mutex guarding attach state and child list plus parent pointer plus CPU placement fields plus owner linkage and task pointer.

Output and control add a mapping mutex plus mapping reference plus ring buffer pointer plus buffer linkage plus RCU batch state plus wait queue plus async notification plus pending wakeup kill disable address and work flags plus deferred interrupt and task work plus an event limit. Filtering adds a filter head plus a resolved range array plus a generation counter plus an auxiliary peer plus a destroy hook plus RCU head plus namespace plus identifier plus lost count plus clock plus overflow handler and context plus BPF state plus optional tracing cgroup and security extensions plus sideband and unit lists plus original type.
Overflow handling uses a callback type whose first argument is the event pointer. The routed line truncates the remainder of the parameter list so arity and further types are not visible here.

A unit context binds a unit to an event context and links into the context list while maintaining separate pinned and flexible active lists. It flags whether storage is embedded in per CPU memory and counts events cgroups and frequency driven events with a reference count plus reclamation head plus a rotation needed indicator for overcommit. Activity holds when either active list is non empty. Groups pair a tree with a monotonic index. Time records current time plus stamp plus offset.

A context centers on a raw spinlock plus a mutex plus a unit context list plus pinned and flexible group trees plus a flat event list. It counts events users active references statistics frequency and rotation state, holds a reference count and an owning task, keeps enabled time and guest time clocks, records parent context plus parent and own generations plus pin count plus optional cgroup count, and tracks a no fast switch count for deferred work and inheritable read samples.

Context lock protects member states plus active counts plus the event list. Either the mutex or the spinlock stabilizes the list for readers while mutation needs both. Event membership changes need the spinlock with RCU safe walks. Sibling and active links need both guards for writes and either for reads. Child attach state uses a dedicated mutex, mappings use another, address filter lists use their head spinlock, unit event lists use their own spinlock, and per CPU timer state uses a timer spinlock.

Context extension data carries a reclamation head plus a reference count plus a global flag plus a slab cache pointer plus opaque storage. Per CPU unit context embeds a unit context plus a task bound unit pointer plus scheduler callback linkage and usage count plus active CPU plus exclusive plus disable counts plus a high resolution timer with its lock interval and active flag.

Per CPU context embeds a full event context plus a current task context pointer plus an online flag plus a small merge heap with a default two entry store. An output handle binds an event to a buffer with wakeup and size plus a flags union covering normal versus auxiliary use and a skip read bit plus an address versus head union plus a page index. Kernel BPF event data bundles registers plus sample data plus the event.

Cgroup timing info keeps enabled time plus guest time plus an active flag. A cgroup record pairs subsystem state with per CPU timing info. Derivation from a task consults subsystem state and requires the context lock to be held when a context is supplied, otherwise proceeding unconditionally, then returns the enclosing record.

Seven small testers inspect branch sampling options for no flags, no cycles, type saving, hardware index, privilege saving, counters, and call stack capture. A companion tester reports whether branch stack sampling is requested at all by looking at the general sample type.

Sample data groups frequently written fields for cache efficiency and is aligned to a cache line. The header carries flags plus period plus dynamic size plus type plus process and thread identifiers plus time plus identifier plus CPU. Optional payload adds instruction address plus callchain plus raw record plus branch stack plus branch counters plus weight plus memory source plus transaction plus user and interrupt register captures plus user stack size plus stream plus cgroup plus address plus physical address plus data and code page sizes plus auxiliary size.
Unavailable memory attribute is expressed by combining not available markers for operation kind plus cache level plus snoop behavior plus lock state plus TLB behavior plus numeric level.

Initialization sets period sampling with the given period and zero dynamic size, adding address sampling only when the address is non zero. Callchain raw and branch savers each run only when the corresponding sample type is requested, warn once on repeated use, and grow dynamic size. Raw totals fragment sizes and pads to eight byte granularity. Branch capture clamps entry count to the configured maximum stack, charges an extra word when hardware indexing is on, and appends counter space when supplied. Total sample size sums the fixed header plus per event header sizes plus dynamic size.

Default overflow is recognized by matching the two built in directional handlers. Exclusion is true when any of idle user kernel hypervisor guest or host exclusion is set. Sampling is true when the sample period is non zero. Software status follows the software capability bit. Software context compares the unit task context number against the software context number. Exclusivity follows the exclusive capability of the unit.

Caller register capture defaults to doing nothing on this architecture while the generic fetcher supplies the immediate caller address. Software events fire only when their static key is enabled, with a scheduler fast path using per CPU register storage. Migration marks the task when migration counting is on. Schedule in processes scheduler events then emits a deferred migration sample and clears the mark. Schedule out emits context switch samples, emits cgroup switch samples only when that counting is on and the derived cgroups differ, then processes scheduler events.
Guest state uses bit zero for active and bit one for user mode, with values one and two.
Guest information hooks provide state query plus instruction pointer fetch plus Intel trace interrupt handling plus mediated PMI handling, allowing the host to attribute samples inside guests.

Snapshot runs in PMI context and must tolerate preemption of start and stop. Filter validation runs in process context without serialization against other unit callbacks so it must be self contained. Filter sync runs during start and depends on caller serialization for list traversal. Output matching runs during open. Sibling walks assume the context assertion and leader check. Duplicate sample sections and use of branch capture without request are diagnosed rather than silently merged.
